problem: Paper tests are slow to grade and give no analytics; Terascore let teachers author, deliver and score tests online.
business_model: Freemium, planned premium at 7 to 9 dollars per month

founders.name: Adam Helybely
founders.background_notes: Previously sold a health education startup with co-founders, per TechCrunch (names not given).

founders.name: Balazs Moldovanyi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch launch article only; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Pearson
competitors.what: Established education publisher and assessment incumbent

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser authoring with math equations, scoring and analytics is standard engineering; planned iPad lockdown mode added some difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Launch coverage says most competition was small point solutions; test building tools were easy to copy.

market_need_then: Beta began mid-February 2013 with five schools creating about 500 tests per week (TechCrunch, 2013-03).

branding.name_origin: Not found. YC lists the company under the name Trainzen while the product and site were Terascore.
branding.domain_note: terascore.com is now parked for sale (GoDaddy) per a 2026 redirect.

rebrands.why: Direction and reason not documented; YC uses Trainzen while launch coverage uses Terascore.

brand_strength.rationale: Two names for one company and no brand coverage; the Terascore name overlaps with unrelated trademarks.

outcome_analysis: Terascore launched in March 2013 as a free online test tool with five beta schools, planning a premium tier at 7 to 9 dollars a month. A secondary site says the idea was not adopted by many schools, and Seedtable calls it not operational. No dated shutdown story exists, so the weak willingness to pay factor is a low confidence inference from the free first model.
notes: terascore.com redirects to a domain for sale. Seedtable says 100K, BizzBucket says 120K (conflict); single-aggregator round, date unknown. YC page lists 3 founders and TechCrunch names four including Moldovanyi, who Latka also calls CEO. Cause of inactivity not public.
